summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Crimea Bridge for the second time in two days, collapsing an automotive arch span and damaging the railway, while Russia launched a massive overnight air attack involving 306 Shahed drones and multiple missile types against targets across Ukraine. Ukrainian air defenses reported destroying 205 Shaheds and several missiles, but strikes hit 44 locations including energy infrastructure in Dnipro and Kyiv bridges, causing heating outages. Russia rejected European participation in upcoming peace talks as Putin convened an emergency meeting over the bridge attack. (Source: DeepStateUA/24005, mon1tor_ua/78391, eRadarrua/131314, UkraineNow/85344, UkraineNow/85350, eRadarrua/131316)
key_points: Ukraine struck the Crimea Bridge again overnight Nov 16-17, collapsing an automotive arch and damaging the railway span, halting all traffic. (Source: DeepStateUA/24005)

Russia launched a massive combined air attack overnight Nov 16-17 using ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, guided aviation missiles, and 306 Shahed drones (92 jet-powered) from multiple directions. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)
Ukrainian air defenses claimed destruction of 205 Shahed drones (48 jet), 3 Kh-59/69 missiles, and 3 Bandero/Dan-T missiles, with hits recorded at 44 locations. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)
Russian strikes damaged Kyiv's Southern and Northern bridges, disrupting heating in Darnytskyi, Obolonskyi, and Podilskyi districts. (Source: eRadarrua/131314)
Dnipro city lost power entirely after attacks on energy infrastructure, affecting water and heating systems. (Source: UkraineNow/85344)
Search operations concluded in Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia) after Nov 2 strike: 72 confirmed dead, 4 missing. (Source: UkraineNow/85347)
Russia refuses European participation in next peace negotiation round, requiring further Ukraine-US-Russia talks first. (Source: UkraineNow/85350)
Putin convened emergency meeting following the second Crimea Bridge attack. (Source: eRadarrua/131316)

sections.executive_summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Crimea Bridge for the second time in two days, collapsing an automotive arch span and damaging the railway, while Russia launched a massive overnight air attack involving 306 Shahed drones and multiple missile types against targets across Ukraine. Ukrainian air defenses reported destroying 205 Shaheds and several missiles, but strikes hit 44 locations including energy infrastructure in Dnipro and Kyiv bridges, causing heating outages. Russia rejected European participation in upcoming peace talks as Putin convened an emergency meeting over the bridge attack. (Source: DeepStateUA/24005, mon1tor_ua/78391, eRadarrua/131314, UkraineNow/85344, UkraineNow/85350, eRadarrua/131316)

points: The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) conducted a month-long, seven-stage special operation to destroy the Crimea Bridge, employing a wide spectrum of Ukrainian-made weapons including Dovbush, Vendetta, Da Vinci, Sich, Mich-2000, Ruta, Palianytsia, An-197, FP-1, FP-5 Flamingo, and R-360 Neptune missiles. (Source: DeepStateUA/24007)

Ukrainian air defense forces intercepted 205 Shahed-type drones (48 jet-powered), three Kh-59/69 guided aviation missiles, and three Bandero/Dan-T cruise missiles during the overnight Nov 16-17 attack, with the engagement involving aviation, missile troops, electronic warfare units, and mobile fire groups. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)

Energy workers in Dnipro are restoring power to water supply, heating systems, and social facilities after the city was completely de-energized following Russian strikes on energy infrastructure, with outages affecting Dniprovskyi, Samarskyi, and Kamianskyi districts. (Source: UkraineNow/85344)

A serviceman in Kyiv region threw a grenade during a domestic conflict in Malaya Berezanka village, killing four people including himself, his mother, his 17-year-old girlfriend, and her mother; the man was reportedly on sick leave. (Source: UkraineNow/85343)

Search and rescue operations in Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia) concluded after two weeks following the Nov 2 Russian strike, confirming 72 fatalities with four persons still missing. (Source: UkraineNow/85347)

Russia launched a massive combined air attack overnight Nov 16-17 using Iskander-M/Zircon/S-400 ballistic missiles from Bryansk, Voronezh, Kursk, and Rostov regions; Iskander-K cruise missiles from Kursk, Rostov, and Orel regions; Kh-59/69 guided aviation missiles from Belgorod region; and 306 Shahed drones (92 jet-powered), Gerbera, S8000 Bandero/Dan-T, and Parodiya decoy drones from Orel, Kursk, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, Shatalovo, Millerovo, occupied Donetsk, and occupied Crimea. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)

Russian strikes damaged the Southern and Northern bridges in Kyiv, causing heating outages in Darnytskyi, Obolonskyi, and Podilskyi districts as heat pipelines were hit, with emergency switching to reserve supply underway for Kurenevka, Obolon, Osokorky, and Poznyaky neighborhoods. (Source: eRadarrua/131314)

Russian attacks on Dnipro energy infrastructure caused a complete blackout across the city, disrupting electricity, water, and heating supplies to residential and social facilities. (Source: UkraineNow/85344)

Russian presidential aide Ushakov stated Russia does not agree to European participation in the next round of peace talks on Ukraine, insisting on further Ukraine-US-Russia negotiation rounds first, despite Europe having designated national security advisors from five countries plus the EU as representatives. (Source: UkraineNow/85350)
Russian President Putin convened an emergency meeting following the second Ukrainian attack on the Crimea Bridge within two days. (Source: eRadarrua/131316)
Russian forces launched multiple cruise missiles from Zaporizhzhia direction toward Nikopol and Zaporizhzhia city, with two Bandero-type missiles reported inbound. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78373)

Ballistic and cruise missiles were fired from occupied Donetsk and Russian border regions toward Kharkiv, Poltava, and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts, including four cruise missiles from Sumy region toward Lubny district and four from Zaporizhzhia toward unspecified targets. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78374)

Russian air defense radar groups detected eight strike UAV groups in Kherson region and five jet UAV groups in Dnipropetrovsk region, indicating intensive drone operations along the southern-eastern axis. (Source: eRadarrua/131306)

A Geran-5 rocket was launched from Kharkiv region toward Poltava district, while jet-powered Shahed drones operated from Dnipropetrovsk toward Kamianske and from Kirovohrad toward Oleksandriia district. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)

Reactive UAVs were launched from Kirovohrad region toward Znamianka and from Cherkasy region toward Uman, showing continued pressure on central Ukrainian logistics. (Source: kpszsu/96895, kpszsu/96894)
Russian forces launched reactive UAVs from Bryansk region toward Chernihiv region, and from Chernihiv region toward Kyiv region targeting Chornobyl area. (Source: kpszsu/96872, kpszsu/96874)

Multiple Shahed drone groups entered northern Ukraine: 10-15 from Chernihiv toward Kyiv's Vyshhorod district, 5 from Kyiv toward Zhytomyr's Korosten district, and 10 from Zhytomyr toward Rivne district. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)

Strike UAV groups were detected in Volyn (1 group), Rivne (2 groups), and Khmelnytskyi (1 group) regions, with reactive UAV groups in Zhytomyr (2 groups) and Chernihiv (1 group). (Source: eRadarrua/131294, eRadarrua/131295)

A reactive Shahed drone was launched from Cherkasy region toward Kyiv's Obukhiv district, and another from Kirovohrad toward Cherkasy district, indicating cross-regional drone routing. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)
Kyiv region air defenses engaged a reactive UAV heading toward Kaharlyk, while Zhytomyr region tracked a reactive UAV toward Ovruch. (Source: kpszsu/96912, kpszsu/96908)

Ukrainian forces conducted a second strike on the Crimea Bridge within two days, collapsing an automotive arch span and damaging the railway track, halting all vehicular, rail, and ferry traffic across the Kerch Strait. (Source: DeepStateUA/24005, DeepStateUA/24007)

Russian missile and drone strikes hit Zaporizhzhia region, with cruise missiles targeting Nikopol and Zaporizhzhia city, and search operations concluding in Komyshuvakha with 72 confirmed dead from the Nov 2 attack. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78373, UkraineNow/85347)
Kherson region saw eight strike UAV groups operating, while Mykolaiv region detected one reactive UAV group and a Bandero missile headed toward Bashtanka. (Source: eRadarrua/131306, kpszsu/96909)

Dnipropetrovsk region experienced five reactive UAV groups and one strike UAV group, with a Shahed drone hitting Kamianske and a Geran-5 rocket launched from Kharkiv toward Poltava. (Source: eRadarrua/131306, mon1tor_ua/78391)

Vinnytsia region tracked UAV groups toward Kryzhopil and Ladizhyn, while Kirovohrad region launched reactive UAVs toward Znamianka and Kropyvnytskyi. (Source: kpszsu/96928, kpszsu/96923, kpszsu/96930)

Russia's overnight Nov 16-17 attack comprised Iskander-M/Zircon/S-400 ballistic missiles (4 launch regions), Iskander-K cruise missiles (3 launch regions), Kh-59/69 aviation missiles (1 launch region), and 306 Shahed drones including 92 jet-powered variants, plus Gerbera, S8000 Bandero/Dan-T, and Parodiya decoys from 7 launch areas. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)

Ukrainian air defense claimed 205 Shahed destroyed (48 jet), 3 Kh-59/69, and 3 Bandero/Dan-T, with cruise missile and 60 Shahed results still being clarified; hits confirmed at 44 locations nationwide. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)

Shahed drones penetrated deep into western Ukraine: 15-20 from Khmelnytskyi toward Ternopil, 10-15 from Chernihiv toward Kyiv, 10 from Zhytomyr toward Rivne, 5 from Kyiv toward Zhytomyr, with strikes reported in Mukachevo (Zakarpattia), Ternopil, Burshtyn (Ivano-Frankivsk), Rivne, Chernihiv, and Kamianets-Podilskyi. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391, mon1tor_ua/78398, mon1tor_ua/78400, mon1tor_ua/78401, mon1tor_ua/78397, mon1tor_ua/78406, mon1tor_ua/78389, mon1tor_ua/78392, mon1tor_ua/78402)

Cruise missiles targeted central Ukraine: 4 from Sumy toward Lubny (Poltava), 4 from Zaporizhzhia, 2 toward Kharkiv, 2 toward Myrhorod/Kremenchuk, and 2 Bandero toward Nikopol/Zaporizhzhia. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78374, mon1tor_ua/78373)

Reactive UAVs launched from multiple vectors: Bryansk to Chernihiv, Chernihiv to Kyiv (Chornobyl), Kirovohrad to Znamianka and Kropyvnytskyi, Cherkasy to Uman and Kyiv (Obukhiv), Zhytomyr to Ovruch, and Kyiv to Kaharlyk. (Source: kpszsu/96872, kpszsu/96874, kpszsu/96895, kpszsu/96930, kpszsu/96894, kpszsu/96912, kpszsu/96908, mon1tor_ua/78391)

key_developments: Ukraine destroyed an automotive arch span of the Crimea Bridge for the second time in two days using Palianytsia missile-drones and Neptune missiles, severing Russia's primary supply artery to occupied Crimea. (Source: DeepStateUA/24007)

Russia executed its largest drone-wave of the war with 306 Shaheds (92 jet-powered) plus missiles across 7 launch zones, overwhelming defenses to hit 44 targets including Kyiv bridges and Dnipro power grid. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)

Ukrainian air defense intercepted 205 Shaheds and 6 missiles but cruise missiles and 60 drones remain unaccounted for, indicating saturation tactics degrading interception rates. (Source: mon1tor_ua/78391)

Kyiv heating infrastructure crippled after Southern and Northern bridge strikes severed heat pipelines, forcing emergency switchover for three districts and temporary hot water loss. (Source: eRadarrua/131314)
Dnipro suffered total blackout after energy facility strikes, halting water, heating, and power to three urban districts and social facilities. (Source: UkraineNow/85344)

Russia formally excluded Europe from next peace talks round, demanding additional bilateral Ukraine-US-Russia rounds first despite EU naming five national security advisors plus EU representative. (Source: UkraineNow/85350)

Putin convened emergency session after Crimea Bridge strike, signaling heightened concern over logistics collapse for southern grouping after Chonhar and Henichesk bridges already down. (Source: eRadarrua/131316)
sections.threat_assessment: Russia's massive combined strike demonstrates sustained long-range strike capacity and intent to degrade Ukrainian energy and command infrastructure ahead of winter. The penetration of Shaheds to Zakarpattia and Ivano-Frankivsk reveals gaps in western air defense coverage. Ukraine's repeated Crimea Bridge strikes systematically isolate Russian forces in Crimea and southern Kherson, but the Kremlin's refusal to include Europe in talks suggests Moscow seeks bilateral deals with Washington while maintaining military pressure. The emergency Putin meeting indicates the bridge loss is operationally significant for Russian southern grouping sustainment.
sections.regional_response: The EU committed to funding Ukrainian customs IT modernization through 2029 via EU4PFM, aligning Ukraine's border systems with EU standards as part of accession preparation. European nations have designated national security advisors for peace talks but face Russian rejection, potentially fracturing Western unity on negotiation format. Regional air defense cooperation remains critical as Shaheds transit multiple countries' airspace en route to targets.
sections.intelligence_notes: The SBU's month-long, seven-stage Crimea Bridge operation using 11 distinct Ukrainian weapon systems reveals sophisticated indigenous defense industrial capacity and operational security. Russian use of Parodiya decoys alongside 306 Shaheds shows evolving saturation tactics to overwhelm air defense tracking. The domestic grenade incident in Kyiv region highlights rear-area instability risks. Komyshuvakha's 72 confirmed deaths underscore the humanitarian toll of Russian strikes on civilian settlements.
